reasoning_traces.think:
Apperception is modeled as a dual-force interaction between a priori conceptual structures (M₁) and a posteriori sensory inputs (M₂), where cognitive synthesis emerges from their dynamic fusion. This process is inherently recursive, with each act of perception modifying prior knowledge. The active-passive duality implies that while conceptual frameworks initiate interpretation, sensory data ultimately shapes understanding. Conceptual enrichment occurs when new sensory data integrates into existing knowledge structures, altering their scope and robustness. In GSI, this maps to Bayesian belief revision where priors are updated with likelihoods to yield posteriors. In GSE, it corresponds to state transitions driven by internal models interacting with external stimuli. The failure mode arises when either component is insufficiently engaged—either conceptual rigidity prevents sensory integration or sensory overload disrupts conceptual coherence.
